newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks carry momentum to record end.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks carry momentum to record end.

text.p: A wave of confidence from overseas investors in Australia's resource and banking sectors on Friday carried local stocks to both a life-time high and a record close.

The All Ordinaries Index closed 19.3 points up at 2,712.6 after reaching an all-time high of 2,714.2 during intraday trading. Over A$1 billion of shares changed hands during the day on turnover of 411 million shares.

"While this market continues to be strengthened by international markets and domestic thoughts that official interest rates may be lowered again, there's really no thought that the trend will take a reversal," said Jamie Spiteri, a Sydney-based dealer with Shaw Stockbroking.
Friday's closing peak was the market's sixth record closing high in the past seven trading days and came after the Dow Jones Index rallied overnight to snap a three-day series of dips.
The local bourse raced through the 2,700 barrier within minutes of opening and surged again just before closing.
Banks were among the outstanding performers, with dealers saying investors were seeking yield stocks. The banking index ended 48.1 points or one percent higher at 4,877.3.
Westpac led the charge to close 18 cents higher at A$8.05 on volume of 3.6 million shares.

BHP profited after analysts revised up their profit forecasts for the blue chip miner and investors backed that judgment. BHP reached a year-high of A$20.05 early in the day and closed up 13 cents at A$19.85 on volume of 6.7 million.

Gold miner Rio Tinto Ltd was one of the few blue chips to buck the trend, losing 42 cents to close at A$22.62. Analysts Rio's fall was in line with a softening in price in Rio Tinto Plc over the past couple of days in London.

Nickel producer QNI Ltd was savaged as investors reacted badly to details of its merger with South African mining house Gencor Ltd. QNI shares fell up to 20 cents before ending nine cents down at A$2.56, with 15.1 million shares traded.
Other dealers said mogul Rupert Murdoch's News Corp had profited from an announcement by loss-making airline Ansett of an alliance with Singapore Airlines Ltd.
Ansett is half owned by News and Air New Zealand. News shares closed three cents up at A$6.28 with 6.6 million traded. (A$ = US$0.75)
